name: Avocados (Hass)
tip: Buy firm, ripen on the counter, then refrigerate once they give slightly to a gentle squeeze.

name: Navel oranges
tip: Heavy for its size means juicy. The 'navel' end should be small and closed.

name: Blood oranges
tip: Moro are the darkest; Tarocco are sweeter with lighter blush. Great in salads and spritzes.

name: Valencia oranges
tip: The juicing orange. A green tinge on the peel is normal (re-greening) and says nothing about ripeness.

name: Mandarins & Pixies
tip: Satsumas kick off in late fall; Ojai Pixie tangerines show up around March.

name: Meyer lemons
tip: Thin, fragrant skin. Zest freely: it's sweeter and floral compared with Eureka lemons.

name: Grapefruit
tip: Oro Blancos and Melogolds are milder, low-bitterness cousins worth seeking out.

name: Kumquats
tip: Eat them whole: the peel is sweet and the flesh is tart.

name: Cherimoyas
tip: Ripe when it yields like an avocado. Chill, halve, and eat with a spoon (skip the seeds).

name: Strawberries
tip: Ask for day-neutral varieties like Albion at the market. Don't wash until right before eating.

name: Loquats
tip: They grow in yards all over LA. Ripe fruit is deep orange and slightly soft.

name: Blueberries
tip: Look for a dusty silver 'bloom', which protects the berry and means it was handled gently.

name: Cherries
tip: Leona Valley, about an hour north, has u-pick orchards for a few short weeks.

name: Mulberries
tip: Too delicate to ship, so markets and backyards are the only places you'll find them.

name: Apricots
tip: Blenheims are the California heirloom. Grab them fast because the season is short.

name: Blackberries & raspberries
tip: Use within a day or two. Spread them on a towel-lined tray in the fridge.

name: Peaches & nectarines
tip: Smell is the best test. Ripen stem-side down at room temperature.

name: Plums & pluots
tip: Dapple Dandy and Flavor King pluots are farmers-market favorites.

name: Figs
tip: Two crops: a small 'breba' crop in early summer, then the main crop in late summer.

name: Melons
tip: A ripe cantaloupe smells sweet at the blossom end and slips off the vine cleanly.

name: Watermelon
tip: Look for a creamy yellow 'field spot' and a deep, hollow thump.

name: Grapes
tip: Try Thomcords or Muscats at the market for flavor you won't find at the grocery store.

name: Prickly pear (tunas)
tip: Handle with tongs or gloves. Singe or scrub off the tiny glochids before peeling.

name: Jujubes
tip: Crisp like an apple when mottled; chewy and date-like when fully brown.

name: Apples
tip: Oak Glen and Julian are the classic SoCal apple towns for u-pick and cider.

name: Asian pears
tip: Unlike European pears, they're ready when bought: crisp, juicy, and great cold.

name: Pears
tip: Ripen at room temp. Check the neck: when it yields to a thumb, it's ready.

name: Quince
tip: Too hard to eat raw. Poach it slowly and it turns rosy pink and perfumed.

name: Pomegranates
tip: Seed them underwater in a bowl: the arils sink, the pith floats.

name: Persimmons
tip: Fuyu (squat) are eaten crisp; Hachiya (acorn-shaped) must be jelly-soft or they're astringent.

name: Pineapple guava (feijoa)
tip: A common LA hedge plant. Collect the fruit that drops, halve it, and scoop.

name: Dates (Coachella Valley)
tip: Fresh-crop Medjools and Barhis show up in fall. A date shake on the drive to the desert is tradition.

name: Artichokes
tip: A squeaky squeeze means fresh. Leaves should be tight and heavy.

name: Asparagus
tip: Snap off the woody ends. Thick spears are often more tender than thin ones.

name: Fava beans
tip: Shell, blanch 1 minute, shock in ice water, then pop the bright green beans from their skins.

name: Peas (English & snap)
tip: Sugar converts to starch fast after picking, so eat them the day you buy them.

name: Green garlic & spring onions
tip: Use the whole thing like a leek, with a gentler garlic flavor.

name: Nopales
tip: Young spring paddles are the most tender. Many LA markets sell them pre-cleaned.

name: Radishes
tip: Eat the greens too. They wilt into pasta or pesto beautifully.

name: Beets
tip: Roast whole in foil and the skins rub right off.

name: Carrots
tip: Cold weather makes carrots sweeter. Remove the tops before storing.

name: Kale, chard & collards
tip: Massage raw kale with salt and lemon for 2 minutes to soften it for salads.

name: Broccoli & cauliflower
tip: Roast hot (450°F) until the edges char. Romanesco works the same way.

name: Brussels sprouts
tip: Buy on the stalk when you can. They keep longer and make a great centerpiece.

name: Cabbage
tip: Keeps for weeks. Thin-sliced with lime and salt, it's a fast taco slaw.

name: Fennel
tip: Shave it raw with citrus, or braise it until it turns silky. Keep the fronds as an herb.

name: Leeks
tip: Split lengthwise and rinse between the layers, because grit hides inside.

name: Lettuces & salad greens
tip: Revive limp greens in a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes.

name: Arugula
tip: Cool-season arugula is milder. Summer heat makes it fiery.

name: Turnips
tip: Small Japanese (Hakurei) turnips are sweet enough to eat raw like apples.

name: Celery root
tip: Peel aggressively and mash half-and-half with potatoes.

name: Squash blossoms
tip: Use the same day. Great in quesadillas with Oaxaca cheese.

name: Zucchini & summer squash
tip: Pick small ones. Big zucchini are watery and seedy.

name: Sweet corn
tip: Look for moist, pale-green husks and sticky brown silk. Cook it the day you buy it.

name: Tomatoes
tip: Never refrigerate. Heirlooms peak in August and September.

name: Cucumbers
tip: Persian and Armenian cucumbers have thin skins and no bitterness.

name: Green beans
tip: They should snap, not bend. Romano and yard-long beans are worth trying.

name: Eggplant
tip: Glossy and heavy is good. Japanese and Chinese varieties need no salting.

name: Peppers & chiles
tip: Hatch-style green chiles show up in late summer. Char them over a burner and steam them in a bag.

name: Okra
tip: Pods under 3 inches are tender. Cook hot and fast to avoid sliminess.

name: Winter squash & pumpkins
tip: Kabocha and delicata are the easiest wins. You don't have to peel delicata.

name: Sweet potatoes
tip: Store somewhere cool and dark, not in the fridge. Japanese purple-skin varieties are extra sweet.

name: Basil
tip: Store it like a bouquet in water on the counter. The fridge turns it black.

name: Cilantro
tip: Bolts fast in summer heat. Grow it in fall and spring in LA.

name: Mint
tip: Plant it in a pot or it will take over your whole yard.
